The sponsor funds every other entry use and owns all common equity throughout. It later receives an interim cash dividend of 150 million dollars. At exit, EBITDA is 250 million dollars and the enterprise multiple is 6 times; debt is 600 million dollars and excess cash is 100 million dollars after the dividend. There are no exit fees, other claims or additional sponsor contributions, and sponsor-level taxes are ignored. What is sponsor MOIC, as an exact multiple?
instances.spoken_text: An investment team combines a dividend with final sale proceeds. At entry, a sponsor buys a business cash-free and debt-free for two thousand three hundred million dollars, pays forty million dollars of cash fees and raises one thousand three hundred million dollars of new debt. The sponsor funds every other entry use and owns all common equity throughout. It later receives an interim cash dividend of one hundred and fifty million dollars. At exit, EBITDA is two hundred and fifty million dollars and the enterprise multiple is six times; debt is six hundred million dollars and excess cash is one hundred million dollars after the dividend. There are no exit fees, other claims or additional sponsor contributions, and sponsor-level taxes are ignored. What is sponsor MOIC, as an exact multiple?

follow_up.question: Why can two investments have the same MOIC but different annual returns?
follow_up.reference: MOIC compares total proceeds with invested capital without using their dates. Receiving the same proceeds earlier raises the annualised return, even though the money multiple is unchanged.
